title: Microsoft Teams Shifts: Assign open shifts fills open shifts automatically
summary: The briefing passes: the optional scheduling workflow, Teams licensing requirement and documented controls are supported. It correctly reports Microsoft's conflicting preview and API documentation; minor corrections should clarify the summary, preserve the notice's planned rollout wording and identify the Graph permission property in the control note.

claims.claim: Assign open shifts automatically fills unassigned shifts in Microsoft Teams Shifts.
claims.quote: Auto Assign Open Shifts is a Microsoft Teams Shifts feature that automatically fills unassigned (open) shifts for you.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The organisation-level Shifts control is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Shifts > Status.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... search for the Shifts app, select it, and then switch the Status toggle to Blocked or Allowed.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> for changing app state.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. ... Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>] ... This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference describes IsBlocked as the app's state in the tenant.
claims.quote: -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. Type: Boolean.

claims.claim: The reference labels examples with IsBlocked $true and IsBlocked $false as unblocking.
claims.quote: Example 3: ... -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app ... Example 4: ... -IsBlocked $false ... Unblocks 1Page App

claims.claim: The documented Status toggle offers Blocked and Allowed choices.
claims.quote: switch the Status toggle to Blocked or Allowed.

claims.claim: Blocking Shifts controls the whole app, including scheduling, swap and time-off functionality, not just Assign open shifts.
claims.quote: A user can't interact with any functionality of an app that the user isn't allowed to use.

claims.claim: The shiftsRoleDefinition API controls which Shifts capabilities frontline managers may configure.
claims.quote: This article describes how you can control permissions to these capabilities using the shiftsRoleDefinition Graph API.

claims.claim: An admin UI for restricting managers' ability to change the Open shifts setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Shifts frontline manager permissions restrict Open shifts shiftsRoleDefinition admin center UI. Opened Manage Shifts permissions for frontline managers and Shifts management; reviewed role and deployment search excerpts. Found API permissions, not an equivalent UI.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The frontline-manager article documents PATCH /beta/teams/{team-id}/schedule/shiftsRoleDefinition/teamowner to update manager permissions.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/teams/fb963991-69a8-4d2c-8465-cd8e374891c4/schedule/shiftsRoleDefinition/teamowner ... "allowedResourceActions": [ "CanModifyShiftRequestsCapabilities"
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: 'The frontline article sets allowedResourceActions; CanModifyShiftRequestsCapabilities controls permission to change Open shifts, Swap shifts and Offer shift settings.' Keep the existing warning about the conflicting Graph reference.

claims.claim: The manager-permissions API is documented under Graph beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state that the Open shifts setting permission governs the Assign open shifts button itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Assign open shifts" disable admin switch PowerShell Graph; Teams Shifts "auto-assign" "disable". Opened feature, manager-permissions and Graph update pages; read shiftsRolePermission excerpt. The documented setting concerns creating/requesting open shifts, not the button.

claims.claim: Graph's update reference gives PATCH /beta/team/{teamId}/schedule/shiftsRoleDefinitions/{roleId}, unlike the frontline article.
claims.quote: PATCH /team/{teamId}/schedule/shiftsRoleDefinitions/{roleId} ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/team/10c2c1cc-6384-48f6-aeba-ef7486344550/schedule/shiftsRoleDefinitions/scheduleowner

claims.claim: Graph's update reference nests allowedResourceActions within shiftsRolePermissions, unlike the frontline article's wrapper.
claims.quote: "shiftsRolePermissions": [ { "allowedResourceActions": [ "CanModifySchedulingGroups", "CanModifyTimeOffReasons" ] } ]
